policy: C1: decide retention, replacement, and retirement from directly overlapping same-task evidence; preserve uncertainty and avoid inferring quality from names, hit counts, or result counts.

comparison_design.task: Return up to five provider metadata records for the same public topic query, artificial intelligence healthcare, for optional literature follow-up.
comparison_design.permission_class: One explicit public read-only request per provider; no account email, secret, credential, or billing action.

crossref.source: Crossref REST API v1 Works query
crossref.top_five_title_pattern: Three returned records share the same title but have different DOIs; one of the five has no provider-reported publication year.

findings: Both adapters completed the same exact public query and returned five provider metadata rows, but at different retrieval times and under provider-specific search and indexing behavior.
The observed top-five DOI sets did not overlap. This is one small ranked snapshot; it does not establish comparative relevance, recall, completeness, metadata correctness, or superiority.
Crossref's returned top five include three distinct DOI rows sharing a title and one missing year. No manual review was performed, so these patterns are not adjudicated as duplicate or invalid works.

Crossref query search has a provider-specific discovery contract. The existing Crossref metadata verifier requires known DOIs and cannot discover them from a topic query; OpenAlex returns OpenAlex Works IDs plus its own metadata and ranking fields.
PubMed, Europe PMC, and arXiv remain separate source-specific query routes. They were not re-run on this exact query in this comparison; no relative-quality conclusion is recorded.

disposition.reason: The observed provider records differ, but this small unreviewed sample cannot establish that one provider is better or covers the other's valuable use cases. Keep the Crossref route default-off and coexist by explicit source scope.
